answer: I would like to talk about someone whose confidence I have always slightly envied. A strikingly confident person I know is a former classmate who now works in sales for a mobile phone company. We studied business administration together, and we were often in the same group for presentations, so I had plenty of chances to watch her in action. From the day I met her, she had this natural [[self-assurance]] that drew people to her. What I find interesting is that her confidence never tips over into arrogance; she is genuinely comfortable in her own skin. As for how she shows it, she can walk into a room full of strangers and start a conversation without the slightest [[hesitation]], which I have always envied. In class presentations, while the rest of us were shaking, she spoke clearly and even enjoyed the difficult questions. I think a lot of her confidence comes from thorough preparation, so she rarely feels caught off guard. She is also unafraid of failure, treating setbacks as [[short-lived]] rather than devastating. Watching her handle difficult situations calmly has taught me a great deal. As for how I feel about her, I admire her enormously. Honestly, I think confidence like hers is partly a personality trait and partly a skill you can build. Being around her is genuinely [[empowering]], because her belief in herself somehow rubs off on the people nearby. I certainly became a better presenter just by watching her, and I still borrow some of her techniques at work.

followUps.answer: More than I used to be. I was quite shy at university, but my job forces me to speak to students and parents every day, and that has gradually helped me [[come out of my shell]].

followUps.q: Do you think confidence can be learned?
followUps.answer: Yes, I believe so. Practice and preparation make a huge difference. The more often you face something that frightens you, like public speaking, the less frightening it becomes over time.
